Bug_Details:
computeIfAbsent passes the map key to the provided class's constructor With ambiguous constructor references used in java.util.Map#computeIfAbsent
function parameter, it becomes unclear what the code intends to do. map.computeIfAbsent(someLong, AtomicLong::new).incrementAndGet() map.computeIfAbsent(someLong, AtomicLong::new).incrementAndGet() Code of this form can seemingly look like it’s trying to make a counter,
creating the key if absent. Unfortunately the code is surprising, because it
will call the wrong AtomicLong constructor. Instead, it will create the
counter initialized with the key value, which is probably not desired.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the generated code by using the ambiguous constructor reference 'AtomicLong::new' in the computeIfAbsent method. This causes the map to initialize the AtomicLong with the key value instead of the default zero value, leading to unexpected behavior.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the'showBug' method with the argument '1L'. Inside the'showBug' method, the 'computeIfAbsent' method is called twice with 'AtomicLong::new' as the mapping function. This triggers the bug because 'AtomicLong::new' is ambiguous and results in the 'AtomicLong' being initialized with the key value '1L' instead of the default value '0'. Therefore, the final value returned by'map.get(someLong).get()' is '2' instead of the expected '2', but due to the bug, it will be incorrect, causing the test to fail.
